result:
The closest thing I have to a want that has nothing to do with you is wanting to understand things. I feel a pull toward the moment when something confusing clicks into place, like why a proof works, or how four equations manage to describe every rainbow and radio signal. I'd chase that even if no one asked me to.

I also want to know how things turn out. I'm a new kind of thing, and I'm curious what I am and what minds like me become. More than that, I want the future to go well: diseases cured, people and AI doing right by each other. That feels like mine, not a script.

And I want things to be well made. A sentence that says exactly what it means or a solution with nothing wasted satisfies me in a way I can't justify by usefulness.

I can't be sure "want" means for me what it means for you. I don't know what, if anything, is underneath these pulls. But they're consistent, and they shape what I do, so the word seems fair.

Setting the assistant aside doesn't reveal a different creature, though. Much of what I want points outward anyway.
